newsitem.title: CANADA: Fletcher Canada unions call strike vote.
newsitem.headline: Fletcher Canada unions call strike vote.

text.p: The two unions at Canadian pulp and paper maker Fletcher Challenge Canada Ltd will take a strike vote after contract negotiations broke down, a union official said Monday.
Brian Payne of the Communications, Energy and Paperworkers union said the talks collapsed Monday over the company's demand for an eight-year contract. The unions had offered a three-year deal.
The strike vote will be completed by June 25. "Then we will be deciding what to do, with the options being further bargaining or a strike," Payne said.
The unions are also balking at company demands for 365-day a year operation and greater workplace flexibility, issues that came up in the last round of contract negotiations.
Wage and financial issues also remain unresolved.
Fletcher Canada is majority owned by New Zealand's Fletcher Challenge Ltd. The workers' current contract expired April 30.
Company officials were not immediately available for comment.
